chapter.title: Furniture; bedding, mattresses, mattress supports, cushions and similar stuffed furnishings; luminaires and lighting fittings, not elsewhere specified or included; illuminated signs, illuminated nameplates and the like; prefabricated buildings

page.h1: HTS Chapter 94: Furniture; bedding, mattresses, mattress supports, cushions and similar stuffed furnishings; luminaires and lighting fittings, not elsewhere specified or included; illuminated signs, illuminated nameplates and the like; prefabricated buildings — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Furniture Exports: Top Buyers, Seats, Lighting & Tariffs
seo.shortDescription: The U.S. exported $9.41B of furniture, seats, lighting and mattresses in 2025; Canada (46%) and Mexico (19%) buy most. Who buys what, and the tariffs.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$9.41 billion** of furniture, seats, mattresses, lighting and prefabricated buildings (HTS Chapter 94) in 2025, down **1.9%** from 2024. Seats and seat parts are the largest group (heading 9401, **$3.67 billion**), led by **seat parts** (9401.99, **$2.20 billion**, the largest single line), then office, bedroom, kitchen and other furniture (9403, **$2.73 billion**), lamps and LED light fixtures (9405, **$1.42 billion**) and medical furniture such as hospital beds (9402, **$796 million**). **Canada** buys **46%** and **Mexico** **19%**; the next buyers, the UK, the Netherlands, Japan and Germany, take about 2–3% each.

Most buyers charge little: qualifying U.S. goods enter Canada and Mexico free under USMCA, the EU has charged **0%** on every U.S. Chapter 94 line since **July 1, 2026**, and Australia is free under AUSFTA. The exception is **Canada**: since **September 8, 2026** it charges a **50%** surtax on U.S. office swivel chairs, metal-frame seats, metal, bedroom, plastic and other furniture and LED light fixtures, and **25%** on upholstered wooden-frame sofas and chairs and wooden kitchen cabinets, with no CUSMA exemption; its global **25%** steel-derivative surtax has also hit U.S. steel office furniture and prefabricated buildings since December 26, 2025. **China** adds **10%** to every U.S. good. Mexico raised its normal rates on most furniture to **25–35%** in 2026, which matters only for U.S. goods that fail the USMCA origin rules.

keyTakeaways: Canada, which buys 46% of U.S. Chapter 94 exports, is the market to watch: its surtaxes now reach most household seating, kitchen cabinets, bedroom and metal furniture and LED fixtures. Seat parts (9401.99), motor-vehicle seats, medical furniture, mattresses and bedding are not on its 2026 list and still enter free under CUSMA.
U.S. sales to Canada fell 6.8% in 2025 to $4.35 billion while Mexico, the second buyer, rose 1.8% to $1.81 billion; January–August 2026 shows the same split (Canada −6.1%, Mexico +6.7%).

The EU dropped its duties on all U.S. Chapter 94 goods to 0% from July 1, 2026 (up to 5.6% before); for wooden furniture the next EU date is December 30, 2026, when the EU Deforestation Regulation starts to apply.
China adds 10% to U.S. furniture on top of a 0% normal rate, and two dates could raise that: December 31, 2026 (tariff exclusions end) and January 10, 2027 (24-point suspension ends).
